question: What happens to unsent, unacknowledged, and re-sent note operations and meeting lifecycle mutations across connection cuts in the real hooks?

scenarios.world: online end to end
scenarios.expectation: baseline: one edit, one acceptance, no duplicates, no divergence

scenarios.world: cold join with the connection cut before the first query
scenarios.expectation: isLoading unresolved and content empty until restore

scenarios.world: server accepted the op; its ack was lost; connection restored
scenarios.expectation: at-least-once re-send DUPLICATES the op on the server and in the reconciled UI

scenarios.world: op queued while offline; connection restored before any server contact
scenarios.expectation: optimistic (consumer) state diverges from saved state while queued; replays exactly once

scenarios.world: participant removed server-side while the consumer is offline
scenarios.expectation: op rejected; consumer keeps the optimistic text with no saved/unsaved signal

scenarios.world: two worlds differing ONLY in server acceptance, compared on the hook's visible state
scenarios.expectation: the hook's visible state is byte-for-byte identical in both worlds

scenarios.world: four consecutive cut/restore cycles, one edit per cycle
scenarios.expectation: duplicates accumulate: every edit is applied twice on the server

scenarios.world: online end to end
scenarios.expectation: baseline: start and end each accepted exactly once

scenarios.world: server started the meeting; ack lost; connection restored
scenarios.expectation: isStarting stays true until the late path; re-send duplicates the start acceptance

scenarios.world: start queued while offline, then navigation away
scenarios.expectation: meeting never starts; the UI believed it did

scenarios.world: end queued while offline, then navigation away
scenarios.expectation: meeting stays active while the user believed it ended; post-call processing never triggered

scenarios.world: server ended the meeting; ack lost; connection restored
scenarios.expectation: re-send duplicates the end acceptance

scenarios.world: prompt-generation action fires while the connection is down
scenarios.expectation: action is not replayed; failure is swallowed (console.warn only, error state null)

scenarios.world: getConnectionInfo called during render with a changing meetingId
scenarios.expectation: render-phase state update loop, capped by React

counts.antiPattern: setCurrentMeetingId called inside getConnectionInfo during render

scenarios.world: registered production handler under convex-test (notes/mutations.ts: applyNoteOperation)
scenarios.expectation: verbatim duplicate (stale expectedVersion) rejected; a re-based duplicate re-applies — clientSequence dedupes nothing [OBSERVED — see results/vitest receipt]
scenarios.observedDuplicateVerdict: verbatim duplicate (stale expectedVersion) REJECTED by the expectedVersion guard; a re-based duplicate (same clientSequence) is ACCEPTED and applied a second time — clientSequence dedupes nothing, content doubled

scenarios.world: registered production handler under convex-test (notes/mutations.ts: applyNoteOperation)
scenarios.expectation: the hook's clientTimestamp shape is rejected by the validator (clientSequence required) [OBSERVED — see results/vitest receipt]
scenarios.observedDuplicateVerdict: n/a — single delivery; confirms hook↔validator arg mismatch

scenarios.world: registered production handler under convex-test (notes/mutations.ts: batchApplyNoteOperations)
scenarios.expectation: stale duplicate rejected; re-based duplicate re-applies with server-side position transformation [OBSERVED — see results/vitest receipt]
scenarios.observedDuplicateVerdict: stale duplicate REJECTED by the expectedVersion guard (seen as CONFLICT after the first batch bumped the version); a re-based duplicate (same clientSequences) is ACCEPTED and re-applies every op with positions transformed server-side — sequence numbers dedupe nothing

scenarios.world: registered production handler under convex-test (notes/offline.ts: queueOfflineOperations)
scenarios.expectation: duplicate accepted: two queue rows for the same operationId, distinct server queueIds [OBSERVED — see results/vitest receipt]
scenarios.observedDuplicateVerdict: duplicate ACCEPTED again — two queue rows for the same operationId (no dedupe; queueIds differ per call)

scenarios.world: registered production handler under convex-test (notes/offline.ts: syncOfflineOperations)
scenarios.expectation: duplicate deduped by the pending->synced status transition; content applied once [OBSERVED — see results/vitest receipt]
scenarios.observedDuplicateVerdict: duplicate DEDUPED by the pending->synced status transition (second sync is a no-op); content applied once

scenarios.world: registered production handler under convex-test (notes/offline.ts: retryFailedOperations)
scenarios.expectation: duplicate retries reject deterministically (nested-sync identity loss under convex-test — harness artifact); exhausted rows excluded silently [OBSERVED — see results/vitest receipt]
scenarios.observedDuplicateVerdict: duplicate retries reject deterministically (UNAUTHORIZED 'Authentication required' — nested sync loses caller identity under convex-test, a harness artifact; transaction rolls back, row untouched); retries on an exhausted row (attempts >= maxRetries) are zero-delta no-ops (retriedCount 0) — silently, with no surfaced error
scenarios.harnessNote: convex-test 0.0.38 does not propagate caller identity into nested ctx.runMutation (get-convex/convex-test#50, open), so a retry whose row-set is non-empty rejects UNAUTHORIZED before the nested sync can run; the post-reset sync behavior is not observable through this harness. Recorded as observed.

scenarios.world: registered production handler under convex-test (meetings/lifecycle.ts: startMeeting)
scenarios.expectation: duplicate rejected by the state guard; no idempotency keys engaged [OBSERVED — see results/vitest receipt]
scenarios.observedDuplicateVerdict: duplicate REJECTED by the state guard ('Meeting is already active') — protection is incidental state-machine ordering, not idempotency (idempotencyKeys rows: 0)

scenarios.world: registered production handler under convex-test (meetings/lifecycle.ts: endMeeting)
scenarios.expectation: duplicate rejected by the state guard [OBSERVED — see results/vitest receipt]
scenarios.observedDuplicateVerdict: duplicate REJECTED by the state guard ('Can only end active meetings') — again ordering, not idempotency

scenarios.world: registered production handler under convex-test (meetings/lifecycle.ts: createMeeting)
scenarios.expectation: duplicate accepted: two separate meeting documents created [OBSERVED — see results/vitest receipt]
scenarios.observedDuplicateVerdict: duplicate ACCEPTED again — two separate meeting documents created (retry after a lost create ack duplicates the meeting)
